title: SREV-028 monitor get uses wrong entry payload size

unicode_string_shape.description: UNICODE_STRING.Length is bytes and does not include a terminating NULL; MaximumLength is total Buffer byte capacity; null-terminated output needs Length + sizeof(WCHAR)

user_buffer_shape.description: User buffers and embedded user pointers must be probed and accessed under structured exception handling

entry_layout.description: Monitor entry header is [Time 8][Type 4][PID 4][TID 4] = 20 bytes; Session_MonitorPutEx writes header then data; Session_Api_MonitorGetEx returns type/pid/tid separately and data through UNICODE_STRING64

shared_header_constant.description: SESSION_MONITOR_ENTRY_HEADER_SIZE names the shared 20-byte header; both writer and reader subtract it when computing data size

reader_gates.description: Reader rejects entries smaller than the header, leaves MaximumLength - sizeof(WCHAR) for terminator, aligns truncated byte count to WCHAR boundary, probes data_size + sizeof(WCHAR), writes terminator at data_size / sizeof(WCHAR)

no_legacy_arithmetic.description: No entry_size - (4 + 4 + 4) payload computation remains; no MaximumLength - 1 byte terminator gate remains

runtime_matrix.description: Windows runtime gate: enable monitor logging, read API_MONITOR_GET_EX through DLL with 256-WCHAR buffer; verify Length excludes header bytes and buffer is NUL-terminated on exact-fit and truncated records

contracts: Writer and reader both reference SESSION_MONITOR_ENTRY_HEADER_SIZE
User-facing UNICODE_STRING64.Length describes only returned data bytes
Truncation preserves a WCHAR terminator slot
Reader probes data_size + sizeof(WCHAR) under exception handling
